title: Schedule toggles can diverge local settings from the Ghostwriter server
reasoning: When Ghostwriter is enabled, SettingsView writes the local enabled period first and only then pushes the change to the server. If updateSchedule throws, the catch block does not undo the local write despite the comment saying it will revert. The app can now display and persist one schedule state while the server keeps generating according to another state.
reproduction: With Ghostwriter enabled, toggle a digest period while the server update fails, for example due to network loss. The local enabled_periods value has already changed, but the server schedule update did not apply.
recommendation: Push to the server before committing local state, or capture the previous enabledPeriods value and restore both @State and UserDefaults if the remote update fails. Surface an error so the user knows the change did not apply.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: SettingsRepositoryTests only cover local schedule persistence; they do not cover SettingsView's two-phase local-plus-remote schedule update or remote failure rollback.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SettingsViewModel/helper test with a mock settings repository and failing Ghostwriter coordinator, then assert enabledPeriods and persisted periods remain unchanged after togglePeriod fails remotely.
minimumFixScope: App/Sources/Views/SettingsView.swift togglePeriod error handling and update ordering.
